title: AWL Sublist 8
description: Las 60 palabras de la sublista 8 de la Academic Word List, con definición, traducción, ejemplo académico, colocaciones y familia léxica.

cards.definition: To leave someone or something permanently; to stop doing or planning something.
cards.example: The project was abandoned after costs rose to twice the original estimate.

cards.definition: To go somewhere with someone; to happen or exist together with something.
cards.example: Rapid economic growth is often accompanied by rising inequality.
cards.warning: Transitivo: "accompany someone", no "accompany WITH someone".

cards.definition: To gradually collect or increase in amount over time.
cards.example: Plastic waste continues to accumulate in the world's oceans.

cards.definition: Having more than one possible meaning, and therefore unclear.
cards.example: Some survey questions were ambiguous, so the responses were difficult to interpret.

cards.definition: To add something, especially extra writing, at the end of a document.
cards.example: A full list of the interview questions is appended to the report.

cards.definition: To recognise the value or importance of something; to be grateful; to increase in value.
cards.example: Few people fully appreciate the role that insects play in food production.
cards.warning: No es "apreciar a alguien" en el sentido de cariño ("be fond of"). "I'd appreciate it if..." = te agradecería que...

cards.definition: Based on chance or personal choice rather than reason or a system.
cards.example: Setting the retirement age at 65 is somewhat arbitrary.

cards.definition: To make a process operate by machines or computers instead of people.
cards.example: Many routine office tasks are likely to be automated within the next decade.

cards.definition: An unfair preference for or against one person, group or idea.
cards.example: Self-reported data may contain bias because people overestimate their healthy habits.

cards.definition: A diagram showing information; to record or follow the progress of something.
cards.example: The bar chart compares household spending in five European countries.
cards.warning: En IELTS Task 1: "The chart shows/illustrates...", no "The chart talks about...".

cards.definition: To make something clearer or easier to understand.
cards.example: This section clarifies the difference between weather and climate.

cards.definition: A product or raw material that can be bought and sold, such as oil or wheat.
cards.example: Economies that depend on a single commodity are vulnerable to price changes.
cards.warning: Falso amigo: "commodity" NO es "comodidad" ("comfort" / "convenience").

cards.definition: To add to something in a way that improves it or makes it complete.
cards.example: Online resources should complement, not replace, classroom teaching.
cards.warning: No confundir con "compliment" (halago), que suena igual.

cards.definition: To behave according to accepted rules or standards; to obey a law.
cards.example: All new buildings must conform to strict energy-efficiency standards.
cards.warning: No significa "conformarse" ("settle for", "make do with").

cards.definition: Belonging to the present time; or living or happening at the same time as something else.
cards.example: Contemporary societies face new ethical questions raised by genetic engineering.

cards.definition: To state the opposite of something; to be so different that both cannot be true.
cards.example: These findings contradict earlier claims that the drug is completely safe.

cards.definition: Extremely important, because it affects what happens in the future.
cards.example: Early diagnosis is crucial to the successful treatment of cancer.

cards.definition: The money used in a particular country; the state of being widely accepted.
cards.example: A weaker currency makes a country's exports cheaper abroad.

cards.definition: To represent or be a sign of something.
cards.example: In the diagram, the dotted line denotes the projected trend.

cards.definition: To notice or discover something that is not easy to see or hear.
cards.example: Modern sensors can detect very small changes in air quality.

cards.definition: To do something different from what is usual, expected or planned.
cards.example: Actual spending deviated significantly from the original budget.

cards.definition: To force people to leave their homes; to take the place of something.
cards.example: Thousands of families were displaced by the construction of the dam.

cards.definition: A play for the theatre, TV or radio; an exciting or emotional situation.
cards.example: Drama classes can help shy students develop confidence in speaking.
cards.warning: Muy útil en IELTS Task 1: "a dramatic rise" / "rose dramatically" = subida espectacular.

cards.definition: Happening at the end of a process or period of time.
cards.example: Poor management led to the company's eventual collapse.
cards.warning: Falso amigo clásico: "eventual" NO es "eventual/posible" ("possible", "potential"). "Eventually" = al final, no "eventualmente".

cards.definition: To show something publicly or show a quality or behaviour; an object shown in a museum.
cards.example: Patients exhibited a wide range of symptoms after infection.

cards.definition: To use something fully for profit; to treat someone unfairly for your own advantage.
cards.example: Some employers exploit migrant workers by paying them below the legal wage.
cards.warning: No significa "explotar" como una bomba ("explode").

cards.definition: To change frequently, especially in amount or level.
cards.example: Oil prices fluctuated between 60 and 90 dollars a barrel during the period.
cards.warning: Clave en IELTS Task 1 para describir subidas y bajadas irregulares.

cards.definition: Official advice or rules on how something should be done.
cards.example: New guidelines recommend at least 150 minutes of exercise per week.

cards.definition: To draw attention to something important; the most interesting part of something.
cards.example: The report highlights the need for more investment in mental health services.

cards.definition: Suggested or understood without being stated directly.
cards.example: There is an implicit assumption that economic growth always benefits everyone.

cards.definition: To cause something to happen; to persuade someone to do something.
cards.example: Stress can induce a range of physical symptoms, including headaches.

cards.definition: Certain to happen and impossible to avoid.
cards.example: Some job losses are inevitable as industries adopt new technology.

cards.definition: The basic systems and services a country needs, such as roads, power and water supply.
cards.example: Poor infrastructure discourages foreign companies from investing in the region.
cards.warning: Normalmente incontable: "infrastructure", no "infrastructures".

cards.definition: To look at something carefully or officially check it.
cards.example: Restaurants are inspected regularly to ensure food safety standards are met.

cards.definition: Very great, strong or extreme.
cards.example: Competition for places at top universities has become increasingly intense.
cards.warning: "Intensive" = que concentra mucho esfuerzo ("intensive course", "intensive farming"); "intense" = fuerte, extremo.

cards.definition: To control or influence people or data unfairly; to handle something skilfully.
cards.example: Advertisers may manipulate consumers' emotions to increase sales.

cards.definition: To reduce something to the lowest possible level.
cards.example: Careful planning can minimise the environmental impact of new roads.

cards.definition: Relating to the energy released by splitting atoms; relating to the nucleus of a cell or atom.
cards.example: Some argue that nuclear power is essential for reducing carbon emissions.
cards.warning: "Nuclear family" = familia nuclear (padres e hijos).

cards.definition: To balance one effect with an opposite one so that the overall result is neutral.
cards.example: The rise in costs was partly offset by higher sales.
cards.warning: Verbo irregular sin cambio: offset - offset - offset.

cards.definition: A section of a text that deals with one idea and begins on a new line.
cards.example: Each body paragraph should begin with a clear topic sentence.

cards.definition: And also; an advantage; more than the number mentioned.
cards.example: The flat costs 900 euros a month, plus bills.
cards.warning: Al inicio de frase ("Plus, ...") es informal: en Writing usa "In addition" o "Moreover".

cards.definition: A person who works in a profession, especially medicine or law.
cards.example: General practitioners are often the first point of contact for patients.
cards.warning: No es "practicante" ("nurse").

cards.definition: Being the strongest, most common or most noticeable.
cards.example: Cars remain the predominant means of transport in most suburban areas.

cards.definition: The possibility that something will happen; future chances of success.
cards.example: Graduates with technical skills have better job prospects.
cards.warning: No es "prospecto" de un medicamento ("leaflet"). "Prospective students" = futuros estudiantes.

cards.definition: Very new and different, or affecting the most basic parts of something.
cards.example: Tackling climate change will require radical changes in how we produce energy.

cards.definition: Happening or chosen without a plan, method or pattern.
cards.example: A random sample of 1,000 households was selected for the survey.

cards.definition: To make an idea, feeling or structure stronger.
cards.example: Advertising can reinforce gender stereotypes from an early age.

cards.definition: To return something to its earlier good condition or position.
cards.example: The aim of the project is to restore wetlands that were drained for farming.

cards.definition: To change something to improve it or make it more accurate; to study again before an exam.
cards.example: Forecasts for economic growth have been revised downwards.
cards.warning: "Revise" implica cambiar o repasar; para "revisar/comprobar" algo suele ser "check" o "review".

cards.definition: A plan listing times when things will happen; to arrange for something to happen at a time.
cards.example: The new line is scheduled to open in 2028, two years behind schedule.

cards.definition: A feeling of nervousness or conflict; a situation where opposing forces exist.
cards.example: There is a tension between economic development and environmental protection.
cards.warning: La "tensión arterial" es "blood pressure", no "tension".

cards.definition: To end something, or to come to an end.
cards.example: The contract can be terminated by either party with one month's notice.
cards.warning: Es formal; para "terminar" algo en general usa "finish" o "end".

cards.definition: The main subject or idea of a talk, book or piece of research.
cards.example: A recurring theme in the interviews was the lack of affordable childcare.

cards.definition: As a result of the action just mentioned.
cards.example: The city expanded its bus network, thereby reducing traffic in the centre.
cards.warning: Suele ir seguido de -ing: ", thereby reducing...". Muy útil para mostrar consecuencias en Writing.

cards.definition: The same in all parts or at all times; special clothes worn by members of a group.
cards.example: Growth was not uniform across the country; the north lagged behind.

cards.definition: A machine for transporting people or goods; a means of expressing or achieving something.
cards.example: Electric vehicles account for a growing share of new car sales.

cards.definition: Travelling through a place; by means of a particular method or person.
cards.example: Data were collected via an online questionnaire.

cards.definition: Almost the same as described; existing on computers or the internet rather than physically.
cards.example: Virtual classrooms allow students in remote areas to access specialist teachers.
cards.warning: "Virtually" suele significar "prácticamente, casi": "virtually impossible" = prácticamente imposible.

cards.definition: Relating to seeing or sight; an image used to explain something.
cards.example: Visual aids such as graphs make complex data easier to understand.

cards.definition: Existing or happening in many places or among many people.
cards.example: There is widespread concern about the effects of social media on teenagers.
cards.warning: Más académico que "very common": "a widespread problem".
